prompt: The bar chart below shows the proportion of household spending on four categories in a European country in 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chartSpec.title: Household spending on selected categories (% of total spending)

modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the share of household spending devoted to four categories in a European country in 2000 and 2020.

Overall, housing and leisure accounted for a larger share of spending by 2020, whereas food became noticeably less important. Transport remained almost unchanged.

In 2000, households spent 28% of their budgets on housing, which rose significantly to 34% twenty years later, so it was the largest category in both years. Leisure saw the second biggest increase, climbing from 10% to 15%, a rise of half.

By contrast, spending on food fell sharply from 24% to 16%. Food had been the second largest item in 2000, but by 2020 it was only marginally above leisure and transport. Transport itself barely moved, edging up from 14% to 15%.

In short, the pattern suggests that households were devoting more of their income to accommodation and free-time activities, while the proportion spent on basic food items declined.
examinerComment: Clear overview, accurate figures and logical grouping of information. Comparisons (rise by half, sharp fall) show good range of data-description language. Avoid personal opinion or explanation not supported by the chart.
usefulPhrases: rose significantly from X% to Y%
a rise of half / a two-fold increase
